Team,

Heads-up: HelioApps (contact: Alicia Gomez) is in final contract negotiations and expects a production start window around 2026-07-01. They just confirmed the initial committed capacity: 24 A100-class GPUs day-one with an expected ramp to ~96 A100-class equivalents over 12 weeks. This is a high-priority late-stage close (HS-789345) — procurement is asking for a capacity attestation before signing.

Please run a capacity availability check and recommendation by EOD Monday (May 31):
- Firm availability by region (us-west-2 / us-east-1 / eu-west-1) for July start;
- Suggested soft-hold quantity (and duration) we can pre-reserve without blocking critical existing commitments;
- Risk analysis (which deals would be impacted if we hold these resources);
- Short remediation/fallback options (quantized model variants, smaller instance families, burst policies).

If we can put a 30-day soft hold on ~24 A100s now (then scale to 36–48 during ramp) that will materially increase our close probability. Tag any proposed holds with the HubSpot deal id HS-789345 and open CAP tickets for ops.

Thanks — need pragmatic numbers, not high-level.

Rishi

Rishi —

Quick inventory snapshot attached (gpu_inventory_snapshot_20260529.csv). High-level findings:
- us-west-2: ~40 A100-class slots currently uncommitted across Dedicated pools (mix of reserved + on-demand capacity).
- us-east-1: ~12 A100-class available, with two near-term commitments in the queue (probable 8–12 weeks).
- eu-west-1: effectively zero A100 headroom for July without rebalancing reserved pools.

Recommendation: place a "soft hold" for 24 A100s in us-west-2 for a 30-day window, with an operational flag to escalate to 36 A100s if DocuSign/SOW is signed. That will leave enough headroom for current committed customers but is tight if another mid-enterprise close surfaces within 2–3 weeks.

Impact: to honor a 36 A100 escalation we may need to delay a scheduled ramp for a Proof-of-Concept (POC) slated for mid-July (POC: MatrixLabs) unless they accept a 2-week later start. I recommend coordination with Account Execs for MatrixLabs if we act on the hold.

Next steps I can do immediately:
- Place the soft hold in the capacity ledger and add the HS-789345 tag;
- Create CAP-1342 (ops ticket) and attach the inventory snapshot;
- Run an availability re-check on Monday morning after we reconcile other ops queue items.

Let me know if you want me to hold in multiple regions (adds orchestration complexity).

Ben Carter

Couple of tactical items from an inference optimization perspective that reduce raw A100 headcount risk:
- Quantization profile: if HelioApps can accept an int8-quantized variant we typically see ~2.5x throughput improvement. For many workloads that can reduce their A100-equivalent need from 96 to ~38–44. See our quantization playbook: https://confluence.redwood.ai/ops/gpu-handbook/quantization-playbook
- Batch/sequence sizing: a conservative batching strategy for production (dynamic batching with a 80–150ms latency SLO) will reduce short-term peak token-rate by ~20–30%.
- Fallback routing: propose a multi-tier route: primary -> A100 pool (soft hold), fallback -> mixed T4 + quantized variants for non-critical batch traffic.

I can draft a short appendix for the SOW explaining the "A100-equivalent" plan and quantization assumptions so Procurement sees a clear technical path in the contract. Also happy to run a quick benchmark with HelioApps sample prompts this week.

Soojin Lee
